items.title: The Gysin pullback of a cycle class and of a coherent sheaf class in the easy cases
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Gysin pullback in two basic situations: the class of a closed subscheme whose intersection with the divisor is again a Cartier divisor, and the class of a coherent sheaf on which multiplication by the defining section is injective (statement lines 5169-5189, tag 02TB). The first part is reduced to the second through the identification of cycle classes of subschemes and structure sheaves, and the second requires a coefficient comparison in a one-dimensional local module where the length of the quotient by the local equation must be matched against a sum over the minimal primes weighted by orders, which is exactly the additivity statement for restricted divisors. That coefficient comparison is the substance, so the claim is H2.
